items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1962-05-07
items.q: I know he had a string band, but I never heard him. ... Joe Petit, Buddy Petit, his father used to play key trombone.

ctx.x: What bands did he play with here? Did he play with a brass band here?

Who was that? John Pellas? Well, I'll tell you the truth. Them times, I don't know what ... I know he had a string band, but I never heard him. But they had two, three bands in the city over here, uptown. And they had a couple of bands down there, the Golden Rule, all of them. Down here we had a couple of bands. Joe Petit, Buddy Petit, his father used to play key trombone. Well, he used to play with Johnny Gould in them. Yeah, he called Joe Petit. That's Buddy Petit's father. Before he was a little kid, the…
You know, I wanted to ask you, I know there's a Johnny Gould, but who was Freddie Gould? Freddie Gould. Did you know him? He's a guitar player? I don't know anything about him.

items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yeah, Joe Petit. Yeah, Joe Petit. All of us used to play key tramoses.

ctx.x: Yeah, Carnish, I know they say Carnish.
Yeah, Joe Petit. Yeah, Joe Petit. All of us used to play key tramoses. Because afterwards, they didn't always get in the slides.
Can you remember anything more about Deucin over across the river, Mooney? Deucin? Did he have any other job or just music?
